transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

That sounds like the hob's overheating protection kicking in. Induction hobs have internal fans to keep the electronics cool, and if those vents are blocked or the fan fails, it will shut down after a few minutes on high power to prevent damage. First, please check that there is nothing blocking the ventilation slots (usually underneath or at the sides of the hob) and ensure there is adequate airflow around it. Also, listen closely when it's running: do you hear a fan noise? If the vents are clear but no fan sound is heard, or if it still cuts out despite good airflow, the cooling fan itself may have failed and will need replacement by an engineer.
yeah fan is loud, seems to roar before it cuts out. not looking under the hob tho. new drawer unit went in under it a month ago if that matters

[Heading: Blocked ventilation from new cabinetry]
That roar confirms the cooling fan is working hard, which strongly suggests the hob is overheating because it cannot get enough airflow. Given you had a new drawer unit installed recently, the most likely cause is that the vents (usually at the front or sides of the hob) are now blocked by the new cabinetry. Please check if there is adequate space around the hob's edges for air to flow freely. If the drawers are touching the hob or leaving very little gap, this will trap heat and trigger the safety shutdown after 5-10 minutes. Clearing that blockage should fix it; if the vents are clear but it still cuts out with a roaring fan, the fan bearing may be failing and would need an engineer to replace.
not pulling the drawer out or lifting the hob, not doing that. is there anything else i can try from on top?

[Heading: Blocked ventilation due to new cabinetry]
Since you aren't able to check under the hob, we have to assume the new drawer unit is blocking the airflow that the roaring fan needs to cool the electronics. This is a very common issue with induction hobs; they rely on that air to dissipate heat from the power modules. Please stop using it on high for now to prevent permanent damage to the internal electronics.
